phases.name: Freeze the spec, cards and targets
phases.why: So nothing we measure or pay for can quietly change later. The files that define the test are fingerprinted, every job has a budget and a stop rule, and the owner has signed the targets.
phases.success: All 6 fingerprints still match. All 11 budget cards pass the kit's card checker (spend cap, GPU-hour cap, stop rule). The owner has signed: under 50 ms per item on one CPU thread; $61.50 planned of $190; pass line = 0.8 x the raters' agreement.
phases.today: Fingerprints match (6 of 6). Cards pass (11 of 11). Waiting for the owner's sign-off.

phases.name: Guideline and gold answer key
phases.why: Every later pass line is set from how well independent raters agree on a fixed answer key. No key means no pass line, and nothing downstream can be called good or bad.
phases.success: At least 30 items, each rated by two independent raters on every question, with agreement and its 95% range written down; the key is frozen with a fingerprint. Marked provisional while models stand in for people.
phases.today: 50 items rated by 4 models (Haiku, Sonnet, Clef, Jev). Agreement between raters: topic 78%, story type 87%, anything changing 70%. Key fingerprint 98f9d7aff3697186. Not yet: a 95% range on the agreement, and a person checking a sample.
phases.how: not yet written; numbers are in runs/p1/jury_agreement.json

phases.name: Agreement between two model families
phases.why: Tells us whether each question is clear enough to train on. If two careful readers disagree, a model cannot be expected to agree.
phases.success: Per question: agreement of 0.6 or more means go; 0.4 to 0.6 means go with a review; under 0.4 means rewrite the guideline.
phases.today: Topic 0.78 and story type 0.87 are go. Anything changing 0.70 is go. Conditions (which of 38) are the weak spot: Haiku and Sonnet overlap 0.59 to 0.64.

phases.name: Qualify the teacher (Haiku)
phases.why: Before we pay to label 25,000 items, prove the cheap labeller is good enough, judged by a model from a different family.
phases.success: On each question Haiku scores at least 0.8 x the raters' agreement, at the low end of its 95% range, against a judge that shares no model family with it.
phases.today: Haiku against the TypeSafe pair (Clef + Jev): topic 82% (low end 68%, line 62%), story type 87% (77%, line 70%), anything changing 69% (56%, line 56%: right on the line). 50 items, so the ranges are wide.

phases.name: Free CPU triage and sample
phases.why: Only about 8 in 100 items report a change in anything. Without a sample that finds them, the rare conditions have too few examples for any model to learn.
phases.success: The sample holds at least 1.5 times as many rare cases as a random sample, with zero near-duplicates of the frozen test.
phases.today: Gate running over 46,775 items (short Haiku prompt; earlier test found 93% of sure changes while flagging 19%). 9 pool items are near-duplicates of the test and are listed to exclude.

phases.name: Pilot, 1,000 items
phases.why: Proves the whole labelling path on 1,000 items for a dollar or two before committing $20 to 25,000.
phases.success: Cost within $1.50; at most 5% of rows rejected; the prompt cache is working; and the gate-chosen half beats the random half on rare cases.
phases.today: Queued behind the gate. Predictions recorded: rejects at most 2%, Haiku about $0.08 per 1,000, flagged half at least 3x the random half.

phases.name: Bulk labelling, about 25,000 items
phases.card: T05 ($20); T06 ($25, only if Haiku fails a question)
phases.why: This is the training set the CPU reader learns from.
phases.success: About 25,000 items labelled with the frozen guideline; at least 30 examples for at least 25 of the 38 conditions; every label records model, guideline version and date; spend within $20.
phases.today: Not started. Estimated cost with Haiku and the gate: about $9 (an estimate).

phases.name: Second-family vote on labels
phases.why: A label is only trusted when two qualified voters agree. Disagreements go to a small review set, not into training.
phases.success: Every voter used passed the pass line on gold; every kept label has at least two agreeing voters.
phases.today: Not started. Jev stage 1 (3 made-up items) and stage 2 (50 gold items) done.

phases.name: Export to Kaggle
phases.why: Puts the training data where the trainer can read it, privately, with the test items kept out.
phases.success: A manifest of fingerprints and counts; overlap with the frozen test is zero.
phases.today: Not started. Kaggle token works; account coreygorman; GPU 10:20 of 30 hours used this week.

phases.name: Train the small CPU reader
phases.why: This builds the thing we are making: a model that reads an item on a CPU instead of calling a large AI.
phases.success: Chosen on dev data only, by a rule written before looking at the test; beats the plain word-count baseline; the 8-bit export loses at most 0.01; at most 3 Kaggle GPU hours.
phases.today: Not started. A free probe suggests a stronger encoder than the 30 MB static model is needed for topic.

phases.name: Score once on the frozen test
phases.why: The one honest pass or fail. It is scored once so it cannot be tuned toward.
phases.success: Per question, the low end of the 95% range is at least 0.8 x the raters' agreement on the frozen 300, and it beats the baseline.
phases.today: Not started. Pass lines (provisional): topic 0.62, story type 0.70, anything changing 0.56.

phases.name: Speed
phases.why: The product only works if it is fast and needs no GPU or API at serving time.
phases.success: Under 50 ms per item on one CPU thread, measured on hardware like production.
phases.today: Not started. Static embedding encode measured at 0.03 ms per item (a part of the pipeline, not the whole reader).

phases.name: Ship decision
phases.why: Decides whether the model leaves the lab, with its card.
phases.success: A clean-environment run gives byte-identical output; the file ships with its card; the owner says go.

phases.name: Wave loop: which guideline wording is stable
phases.why: Find which wording of the guideline gives stable answers before labelling at scale.
phases.success: Two rounds in a row move topic agreement by less than 0.015.
phases.today: Met: waves 9 to 17 moved it by 0.013 then 0.003. Stopped; guideline frozen at the wave-5 version. Cost $33.80 of $50. Condition agreement did not improve.
